trial.title: Evaluation of the Clinical and Cost-effectiveness of an Automated Mobile Hybrid Room in Vascular Surgery Compared with Current Practice

endpoints.measure: Cost consequence analysis associated with endovascular procedures performed using automatic imaging fusion guidance and conventional endovascular technique performed without image fusion guidance up to 30 days time horizon and a collective perspective.
endpoints.description: To compare the costs and consequences associated with endovascular procedures performed using automatic imaging fusion guidance and conventional endovascular technique performed without image fusion guidance. Consequences are listed in the secondary endpoints. Cos twill be express in €.

outcome.rationale: Cydar-EV fusion guidance has consistent evidence for reducing radiation exposure, contrast use, and procedure time from sister ARIA trial and meta-analyses. Secondary endpoints likely favor fusion. Primary cost endpoint uncertain but efficiency gains support potential cost-effectiveness. Trial expected to demonstrate clinical and economic benefits of fusion guidance.

analysis_trace: Trial NCT06590532 is a French RCT evaluating Cydar-EV automated image fusion vs standard X-ray fluoroscopy for EVAR/aorto-iliac procedures. Primary endpoint is cost consequence analysis; secondary endpoints include radiation dose, contrast dose, ITU/HDU stay, technical/clinical success, 30-day mortality, QoL, and cost-effectiveness.

Evidence retrieved: ARIA trial protocol (ISRCTN13832085) and statistical analysis plan (PMC12042510) describe the UK sister trial using same Cydar-EV technology. King's College London reports (2022) cite mean 35% reduction in fluoroscopy time, 41% reduction in contrast, 1-hour reduction in operating time with Cydar-EV.

Meta-analysis evidence (SAGE JEVT 2020) shows image fusion significantly reduces contrast volume, fluoroscopy time, and procedure time in complex EVAR; reduces contrast and procedure time in standard EVAR. Radiation dose reduction suggested but not consistently significant across all studies.

Evidence role assessment: ARIA protocol and KCL reports provide indirect_direction for Cydar-EV benefits on radiation/contrast/procedure time. Meta-analysis provides indirect_direction for fusion imaging benefits. No direct results from NCT06590532 available before cutoff.

Population match: ARIA trial (UK) and NCT06590532 (France) both use Cydar-EV for EVAR with similar inclusion criteria (elective AAA, trained surgeons). Evidence_role: indirect_direction with good generalizability.

Primary endpoint (cost consequence): No direct cost data available. Based on ARIA trial design and reported efficiency gains (shorter procedure time, reduced complications), fusion guidance likely cost-effective but exact magnitude uncertain. Predicted direction: favorable to fusion group.
Secondary-0 (X-ray dose): Evidence supports reduction. Predicted mean reduction 25-40% vs control based on prior Cydar studies. Confidence moderate.
Secondary-1 (physician X-ray dose): Operator exposure parallels patient dose reduction. Predicted mean reduction 25-35%.
Secondary-2 (contrast dose): Strong evidence for reduction. Meta-analysis and KCL data support ~40% reduction. Confidence higher.
Secondary-3 (ITU/HDU stay): No direct evidence. Elective EVAR typically has low ITU admission. Predicted no significant difference between groups.
Secondary-4 (technical success): Fusion improves visualization and positioning. Predicted higher technical success in fusion group, but both groups expected high success (>95%).
Secondary-5 (clinical success): 1-month patency/exclusion expected high in both groups. Fusion may have slight advantage due to better positioning.
Secondary-6 (30-day mortality): Elective EVAR mortality typically 1-2%. No expected difference between groups.
Secondary-7 (QoL): EQ-5D-5L at 30 days. No expected difference; both groups minimally invasive.
Secondary-8 (5-year cost-effectiveness): Long-term projection; based on efficiency gains and reduced reinterventions, likely favorable to fusion but highly uncertain.
Key uncertainties: No direct French trial results; cost data not available; long-term outcomes speculative; trial still recruiting at cutoff.
